headline: Microsoft barred from sponsoring foreign workers for US residency by Trump admin
summary: The US government claims Microsoft abused immigration programs, temporarily banning it and other tech giants from sponsoring permanent residency for foreign workers.
details: The Trump administration has temporarily banned Microsoft, Adobe, and six other IT outsourcing companies from sponsoring foreign workers for permanent US residency. The administration claims these companies abused immigration programs, specifically the H-1B visa program, at the expense of American citizens.

Vice President JD Vance stated that the H-1B visa program has become "rife with fraud" and that over-reliance on these schemes is "a fundamental insult to the American worker." He specifically called out Microsoft, alleging it "laid off last year 6,000 American workers at the same time the company benefited from 6,300 H-1B visas and almost 3,000 green cards."

Microsoft has disputed the claims, stating that the "vast majority" of its US employees are American and that the visa applications mentioned were largely "to extend or change the status" of existing employees. The company asserts it only files H-1B petitions for those who meet the program's rigorous standards.
The ban also affects Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, and Capgemini. The Labor Department Inspector-General confirmed that investigations are underway and "nobody will be getting a free pass."

The Indian government reacted angrily to the terminology used by Vance, calling descriptions like "foreign indentured servants" deeply offensive and unwarranted, highlighting the contributions of Indian professionals to the US economy.

This move is part of a broader crackdown on immigration by the Trump administration, which has previously targeted H-1B visas. While the impact on the overall number of visas may be small due to existing backlogs for permanent residency, it signals a stricter stance on foreign worker sponsorship.
Microsoft shares dropped over 1 percent following the announcement. The company maintains its commitment to hiring locally and adhering to visa regulations.
